# Resource: stripe_topup

A top-up of your Stripe balance from your bank account. Set `status` to `canceled` to cancel a top-up that is still pending. Stripe moves a pending top-up to `succeeded` by itself. Only `description` and `metadata` change after creation.

~> A topup can move real money. In a live-mode Stripe account, creating or changing one, including setting its `status`, fails at plan time unless the provider sets `allow_live_money_movement = true`. Reading or importing one never does. The provider asks Stripe for the account's mode. See the Managing Test Data guide.

~> Stripe cannot delete a top-up; set `status` to `canceled` to cancel a pending one. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the topup, fail at plan time. To stop managing a topup, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Add test funds to the balance from the account's bank account.
resource "stripe_topup" "funds" {
  amount      = 100000
  currency    = "usd"
  description = "Test funds"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `amount` - (Required) A positive integer representing how much to transfer. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `currency` - (Required) Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.

The following arguments are optional:

* `description` - (Optional) An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `payment_method` - (Optional) The ID of a PaymentMethod representing the payment method to be used for the top-up. A PaymentMethod of type `us_bank_account` can be used. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `payment_method_options` - (Optional) Payment method-specific configuration for this top-up. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. See [`payment_method_options`](#payment_method_options) below.
* `statement_descriptor` - (Optional) Extra information about a top-up for the source's bank statement. Limited to 15 ASCII characters. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `status` - (Optional) The status of the top-up is either `canceled`, `failed`, `pending`, `reversed`, or `succeeded`. Possible values: `canceled`.
* `transfer_group` - (Optional) A string that identifies this top-up as part of a group. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.

<a id="payment_method_options"></a>
### `payment_method_options`

The `payment_method_options` attribute supports:

* `us_bank_account` - (Optional) If this top-up is to be used with a `us_bank_account` payment method, this sub-hash contains configuration for it. See [`payment_method_options.us_bank_account`](#payment_method_options.us_bank_account) below.

<a id="payment_method_options.us_bank_account"></a>
### `payment_method_options.us_bank_account`

The `payment_method_options.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `network` - (Required) The US bank transfer network used for this top-up. The default is `ach`. Possible values: `ach`.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `balance_transaction` - ID of the balance transaction that describes the impact of this top-up on your account balance. May not be specified depending on status of top-up.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `expected_availability_date` - Date the funds are expected to arrive in your Stripe account for payouts. This factors in delays like weekends or bank holidays. May not be specified depending on status of top-up.
* `failure_code` - Error code explaining reason for top-up failure if available (see [the errors section](https://docs.stripe.com/api/errors) for a list of codes).
* `failure_message` - Message to user further explaining reason for top-up failure if available.
* `initiated_by` - Indicates whether the top-up was initiated by Stripe or by the user. Possible values: `stripe`, `user`.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `source` - The source field is deprecated. It might not always be present in the API response. See [`source`](#source) below.

<a id="source.receiver"></a>
### `source.receiver`

The `source.receiver` attribute supports:

* `address` - The address of the receiver source. This is the value that should be communicated to the customer to send their funds to.
* `amount_charged` - The total amount that was moved to your balance. This is almost always equal to the amount charged. In rare cases when customers deposit excess funds and we are unable to refund those, those funds get moved to your balance and show up in amount_charged as well. The amount charged is expressed in the source's currency.
* `amount_received` - The total amount received by the receiver source. `amount_received = amount_returned + amount_charged` should be true for consumed sources unless customers deposit excess funds. The amount received is expressed in the source's currency.
* `amount_returned` - The total amount that was returned to the customer. The amount returned is expressed in the source's currency.
* `refund_attributes_method` - Type of refund attribute method, one of `email`, `manual`, or `none`.
* `refund_attributes_status` - Type of refund attribute status, one of `missing`, `requested`, or `available`.

<a id="source.redirect"></a>
### `source.redirect`

The `source.redirect` attribute supports:

* `failure_reason` - The failure reason for the redirect, either `user_abort` (the customer aborted or dropped out of the redirect flow), `declined` (the authentication failed or the transaction was declined), or `processing_error` (the redirect failed due to a technical error). Present only if the redirect status is `failed`.
* `return_url` - The URL you provide to redirect the customer to after they authenticated their payment.
* `status` - The status of the redirect, either `pending` (ready to be used by your customer to authenticate the transaction), `succeeded` (successful authentication, cannot be reused) or `not_required` (redirect should not be used) or `failed` (failed authentication, cannot be reused).
* `url` - The URL provided to you to redirect a customer to as part of a `redirect` authentication flow.

The `source.source_order` attribute supports:

<a id="source.source_order.items"></a>
### `source.source_order.items`

The `source.source_order.items` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - The amount (price) for this order item.
* `currency` - This currency of this order item. Required when `amount` is present.
* `description` - Human-readable description for this order item.
* `parent` - The ID of the associated object for this line item. Expandable if not null (e.g., expandable to a SKU).
* `quantity` - The quantity of this order item. When type is `sku`, this is the number of instances of the SKU to be ordered.
* `type` - The type of this order item. Must be `sku`, `tax`, or `shipping`.

* `name` - Recipient name.
* `phone` - Recipient phone (including extension).
* `tracking_number` - The tracking number for a physical product, obtained from the delivery service. If multiple tracking numbers were generated for this purchase, please separate them with commas.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing a topup whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_topup.funds

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_topup.funds
```

The topup stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a topup using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_topup.funds
  id = "tu_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_topup.funds
  identity = {
    id = "tu_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the topup.

Using `terraform import`, import a topup using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_topup.funds tu_123
```
